thread.title: Soccer rules panel clarifies VAR process that World Cup red card for Switzerland's Embolo was wrong
thread.title_full: Soccer rules panel clarifies VAR process that World Cup red card for Switzerland's Embolo was wrong

author: AP
title: Soccer rules panel clarifies VAR process that World Cup red card for Switzerland's Embolo was wrong
text:
• Soccer's law-making panel clarified its guidance to referees which confirmed Switzerland forward Breel Embolo shouldn't have been sent off in the World Cup quarterfinals against Argentina.
• Embolo's second yellow card after a video review was for simulating being fouled.
• Argentina's Leandro Paredes had been shown a yellow card until VAR officials alerted the referee.
• It changed the game soon after Switzerland tied the score at 1-1.
• Argentina's 3-1 win after extra time fueled complaints referees were favoring Lionel Messi’s team.
• The rules panel IFAB has clarified VAR protocol for “mistaken identity” is not yet eligible for an Embolo-type incident.
• Zinedine Zidane is France’s new coach.
• He replaces Didier Deschamps at the helm of the team he led to glory as arguably its greatest ever player.
• French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo has announced Zidane’s appointment at the FFF headquarters in Paris on Tuesday.
• “I’ve waited five years for this chance, so that’s why I’m a bit emotional,” Zidane says.
• He has been given a 4-year contract.
• Diallo says, “Zinedine is one of the legends of French soccer and for many years he said one of his dreams was to take charge of the France team.”
• The 54-year-old Zidane has not coached since leaving Real Madrid in 2021.
• Roberto Mancini has once again been tasked with revitalizing an Italy team in crisis.
• Italian soccer federation Giovanni Malagò announced Mancini as the new Italy coach on Tuesday.
• He added that Claudio Ranieri will become the new technical director.
• Italy has failed to qualify for the past three World Cups.
• Mancini led the Azzurri to the European Championship title in 2021 but shockingly resigned as Italy coach in August 2023, taking over Saudi Arabia’s national team two weeks later.
• There will be a press conference on Wednesday with Mancini and Ranieri.
• The Texas Rangers have put themselves in a good position in the AL West just by having a winning record.
• At 54-52, Texas is the only team in the division not under .500 with about one-third of the regular season remaining, and now less than a week before next Monday’s trade deadline.
• The Rangers are the AL West leader by two games ahead of in-state nemesis Houston.
• They are 2 1/2 games in front of reigning division champion Seattle after taking three of four against the Mariners.
• Seattle has lost 11 of its last 16 games.
• Authorities in Loudoun County, Virginia, have arrested the son of Chiefs assistant coach Eric Bieniemy and charged him in the shooting of his mother.
• Elijah Zion Bieniemy was booked into the Loudoun County Adult Detention Center on Monday.
• Deputies responded to a shooting in Ashburn, Virginia, late Sunday.
• They found 57-year-old Mia Bieniemy with multiple gunshot wounds.
• She was taken to a hospital and was in stable condition.
• The 27-year-old Elijah Bieniemy faces charges including malicious wounding and use of a firearm in a felony.
• He is being held without bond.
• The Chiefs have acknowledged the incident, offering thoughts and prayers for the family.
• The award, given annually to the top female college athlete, celebrated its 50th anniversary Monday.
• Ann Meyers Drysdale felt nostalgic spending the day with so many other Honda Cup award winners, including fellow UCLA Bruins great Jackie Joyner-Kersee.
• Chamique Holdsclaw still fondly remembers meeting the best female college athletes in their respective sports when she won the Honda Cup in 1998 while starring at Tennessee.
• Out of all the individual sport winners, an overall Athlete of the Year is chosen.
• In addition to athletic performance, the Honda Cup honors college athletes for their leadership, academics and community service.
• FIFA President Gianni Infantino has attacked perceived critics one week after the World Cup final for “spreading hate and false rumors” about the tournament.
• Infantino praises FIFA for “delivering the best show in the world” and spoke of the World Cup bringing “joy and togetherness.”
• He also rounds on critics in a 900-word statement published in a 15-page post on Instagram and FIFA’s website.
• The FIFA leader writes “sorry that you were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all.”
• Infantino has an increasingly testy relationship with media in the 11th year of his presidency.
• New York Yankees outfielder Cody Bellinger will be sidelined for four to six weeks with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain.
• Bellinger was placed on the 10-day injured list on Sunday, a day after he got hurt running the bases during a 3-1 win at Philadelphia.
• He had more tests in New York that revealed the extent of the injury.
• The loss of Bellinger is another major injury for a New York team already playing without reigning AL MVP Aaron Judge, who has been out since May 31 because of a fractured rib.
• Designated hitter Giancarlo Stanton has been sidelined since April 24 because of a strained right calf.
• The Marlins finally won a game.
• Miami overcame two-run, ninth-inning deficit in the ninth to beat division-rival Philadelphia and snap a 12-game losing streak — the longest such stretch in franchise history.
• It was the Marlins’ first win since beating Seattle at home on July 9 and ensured they would not suffer their fifth straight sweep.
• Griffin Conine singled in the winning run against Philadelphia closer Jhoan Duran, who entered in the ninth with a 7-5 lead before loading the bases with no outs.
• The College Football Players Association has announced that Stanford has become the first team to organize a player-led chapter.
• The group advocates for unionization and collective bargaining.
• CFBPA executive director Jason Stahl says the goal is for other Atlantic Coast Conference schools to join Stanford.
• This could create momentum for unionization and bargaining over working conditions.
• Stanford players elected offensive lineman Fisher Anderson and linebacker Ernest Cooper as their representatives.
• Anderson believes the CFPA will give players a voice in governing college football.
• The NCAA and conferences are working with Congress on a Senate bill for an antitrust exemption.
